cards.text: Letter time, friend. The writer of Hebrews is writing to believers about the sacrifices offered under the law, and he opens with a picture: the law is only a shadow.

cards.question: The writer of Hebrews calls the law only a shadow. A shadow of what?

cards.text: A shadow, "not the realities themselves." I once tried to grab a cookie's shadow off my counter with my mustache, and friend, I grabbed that counter FIVE times before I let it go.

cards.question: Under the law, the same sacrifices are offered year after year. The writer says those sacrifices can make the worshipers perfect.
If those sacrifices could make worshipers perfect, what does the writer say would have happened to the offerings?

cards.text: Think about it. If those sacrifices really worked, the worshipers would have been cleansed for good and would no longer have felt the guilt of their sins.

cards.question: But the sacrifices keep coming. The writer says those sacrifices are an annual ___ of sins.

cards.text: Here's why: "it is impossible for the blood of bulls and goats to take away sins." So it's like a phone alert that pops up every year yelling YOUR BILL IS DUE, and that alert has never once paid the bill.
So when Christ came into the world, He spoke to God about all this. He said sacrifice and offering weren't what God desired.

cards.question: Instead of sacrifice and offering, Christ says God prepared a body for Him.
Christ keeps speaking to God. Which offerings does He say God took no delight in?

cards.text: Then Christ says, "Here I am, it is written about Me in the scroll." No more shadows, friend. Now we're talking about the real thing.

cards.question: God didn't desire those sacrifices. So when Christ says Here I am, what does He say He has come to do?

cards.text: Then the writer walks back through that quote. God didn't desire those sacrifices, even though they're offered according to the law, and then Christ adds that He has come to do God's will.

cards.question: Talking about the old sacrifices and doing God's will, the writer says: He takes away the first to establish the ___.

cards.text: And here's the payoff, friend. By that will, the writer says, we have been sanctified through the sacrifice of the body of Jesus Christ.

cards.question: The old sacrifices came year after year. But the body of Jesus Christ was sacrificed ___ for all.

cards.text: Day after day, every priest stands to minister and offers the same sacrifices again, and again, and AGAIN. And not one of those sacrifices can ever take away sins.

cards.question: Every other priest keeps standing and offering. But after Jesus offered one sacrifice for sins for all time, what did He do?

answers.text: He sat down at the right hand of God
He stood to offer another one
He went back into the temple

cards.question: Since that time, Jesus waits for His enemies to be made a footstool for His feet.
The law could never do it, but by a single offering Jesus has made ___ for all time those who are being sanctified.

cards.text: Then the writer calls in another witness: the Holy Spirit testifies about this too. First the Spirit speaks of a covenant the Lord declares He will make "after those days."

cards.question: In this new covenant, where does the Lord say He will put His laws?
In this covenant, the Lord says He will remember their sins and lawless acts every year.

cards.text: Friend, I spent YEARS forgotten in the back of a junk drawer, so I never had one nice word to say about forgetting. But the Lord saying their sins and lawless acts He will remember no more? That's the best forgetting I ever heard of.

cards.question: Where sins have been forgiven, what does the writer say is no longer needed?

findings.problem: Stop 1, card 12 quotes "Here I am, it is written about Me in the scroll.", which isn't the exact BSB wording.

rule.text: Quotes: Quotation marks around Bible words mean the exact BSB wording, punctuation included.

findings.problem: Stop 2, card 5 quotes "after those days.", which isn't the exact BSB wording.

rule.text: Quotes: Quotation marks around Bible words mean the exact BSB wording, punctuation included.

findings.problem: The question asks the baker to guess which kinds of offerings are named in the quoted line. Nothing in the earlier cards lets a baker reason between burnt and sin offerings, grain and drink offerings, or peace and wave offerings. It is the same kind of detail-guessing as the bad Psalm 23 example (oil, myrrh or perfume).

rule.text: Ask about the movement and the meaning: what changes, what the picture is, why the speaker says what he says.

findings.problem: The wrong answers can be argued right from the passage. Hebrews 10:5 and 10:8 say God did not desire or delight in sacrifices and offerings in general, not only burnt and sin offerings. Grain and drink offerings are offerings, and peace offerings are sacrifices, so a baker could argue that God took no delight in them either.

rule.text: Each wrong answer must be false anywhere in the passage, not just at that moment.

findings.problem: The setup inside the question ('The old sacrifices came year after year. But the body of Jesus Christ was sacrificed ___ for all.') rules out the wrong answer 'yearly' through the contrast. That leaves only 'once' and 'daily'.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: The setup ('Every other priest keeps standing and offering. But after Jesus offered one sacrifice for sins for all time') rules out the wrong answer 'He stood to offer another one'. The contrast with standing also points straight to sitting.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: 'The law could never do it' uses 'it' to point back to Stop 1, card 4 (making worshipers perfect), which is no longer on screen. The question doesn't say what 'it' is.

rule.text: Always give context in the question. The story card before it isn't on screen anymore, so the question says who and what. Never "him," "that" or "it" pointing back to a card the baker can't see.

findings.problem: The question calls it 'this new covenant'. Hebrews 10:16 says only 'the covenant I will make with them after those days' and never uses the word 'new' in this passage.

rule.text: Call things what the text calls them.

findings.problem: This story card has three sentences ('Friend, I spent YEARS…' / 'But the Lord saying…?' / 'That's the best forgetting I ever heard of.').

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: The card only retells Hebrews 10:17, which card 7 already covered, and adds a reaction. It doesn't move the baker forward to anything new in the passage, so it works as a recap card with a joke attached.
Most story cards read as plain summaries with no Papa Dorin humor or energy: Stop 1 cards 6, 9, 14 and 16, and Stop 2 cards 1 and 5. Only three cards in the whole walkthrough have a real laugh.

rule.text: When a moment can hold a real laugh without muddying a fact, he goes for it. If a line reads like a nice dad being pleasant, push it further.
